ex.s: According to this theory, people approach digital texts with a mindset suited to social media, which are often not so serious, and devote less mental effort than when they are reading print.
ex.t: 根据这一理论，人们以一种适合社交媒体的心态对待电子文本——往往不那么严肃，投入的脑力也比读纸质文本时少。

ex.s: Readers treat digital texts lightly.

ex.s: Clearly, my way of reading the text had shifted, and I myself had changed over the years.
ex.t: 显然，我阅读文本的方式已经改变，而这些年来我自己也变了。

ex.s: This kind of planned revisit could also be for confirming certain details in the text, or for checking on the moves of a given character.
ex.t: 这种有计划的重读也可以是为了确认文本中的某些细节，或者查看某个特定人物的动向。

ex.s: The original reading was either forgotten or so totally absorbed that the new chance encounter with the text produced surprise and astonishment.
ex.t: 最初的阅读要么被遗忘了，要么被完全吸收，以至于再次偶然遇到这段文字时产生了惊讶和震撼。

ex.s: If you want to tell the history of the whole world, a history that does not privilege one part of humanity, you cannot do it through texts alone, because only some of the world has ever had texts, while most of the world, for most of the time, has not.
ex.t: 如果你想讲述整个世界的历史，一部不偏袒任何一部分人类的历史，你就不能只依靠文字文献，因为世界上只有一部分地区曾经有过文字，而世界上大部分地区在大部分时间里都没有。

ex.s: By translating the rich and humourous text of Love’s Labour’s Lost into the physical language of BSL, Deafinitely Theatre creates a new interpretation of Shakespeare’s comedy and aims to build a bridge between deaf and hearing worlds by performing to both groups as one audience.
ex.t: 通过将《爱的徒劳》丰富幽默的文本翻译成英式手语这种肢体语言，Deafinitely剧院为莎士比亚的喜剧创造了一种新的诠释，并旨在通过为聋人和听力正常的人共同演出，在两者之间架起一座桥梁。

ex.s: The benefits of print reading particularly shine through when experimenters move from posing simple tasks — like identifying the main idea in a reading passage — to ones that require mental abstraction — such as drawing inferences from a text.

ex.s: If we are to find the other half of that conversation, we have to read not just the texts, but the objects.
